description: Two tools that operate outside the normal running order. Closers widen the aperture and leave the guest with a good last taste. Pivots are emergency equipment - keep them visible on the page and reach for one the moment a guest slips into talking points or an answer dies.

questions.text: What is a question you wish people asked you about your work?
questions.lands_because: Hands the guest the microphone and frequently produces the best two minutes of the episode. It also stocks your database - whatever they name, add it.

questions.text: If you could change one thing about your field, what would it be?
questions.lands_because: Standard but effective. It works better if you follow immediately with the constraint question, which is what turns an easy wish into a real analysis.

questions.text: What are you still trying to get better at?
questions.lands_because: Works on the most senior guest in any field, and the answer is almost always more specific and more humble than expected.

questions.text: Who should I talk to next, and what should I ask them?
questions.lands_because: Books your next guest and writes the first question for that episode. The second clause is the valuable half - do not drop it.

questions.text: What should someone who wants your job know that nobody tells them?
questions.lands_because: Directs the guest's expertise at a real audience member rather than at the abstract public, which tends to make the advice concrete instead of inspirational.
followups: What would you tell them not to worry about?

questions.text: Let me ask that a different way - give me one specific instance.
questions.lands_because: The workhorse pivot. Abstraction is where evasion lives; a demand for one instance dissolves it without any confrontation.
followups: When was that? Who else was in the room?

questions.text: That is the answer you would give publicly. What is the more complicated one?
questions.lands_because: Names the talking point without accusing the guest of dishonesty, and offers complexity as a flattering alternative. Delivered warmly, it usually works.
questions.avoid_if: You have used it once already in the episode, or the guest is genuinely constrained by legal or regulatory limits rather than being evasive.

questions.text: Who would disagree with what you just said, and what is their best argument?
questions.lands_because: Introduces conflict without you having to supply it, and asking for the opponent's *best* argument produces a much better answer than asking for the disagreement alone.
followups: Where do they have a point?

questions.text: Can you put a number on that?
questions.lands_because: Converts vague scale claims - a lot, very fast, huge - into something the audience can hold. Five words and it sharpens any answer.
followups: Is that typical, or was that an unusual one?

questions.text: You said {phrase} - what does that actually look like on a Tuesday?
questions.lands_because: Takes jargon the guest used without noticing and grounds it in observable behavior. Fill the slot with their own words - the echo is what makes it land.

questions.text: What am I not asking about that I should be?
questions.lands_because: Works as a mid-episode reset when a line of questioning is not producing, and often redirects to the thing the guest actually came to talk about.
